docs.title: GDS-ParT: Gated Dual-Stream Particle Transformer
docs.text:
GDS-ParT is a PyTorch transformer for jet tagging on the JetClass benchmark. It explores another way of feeding pairwise particle physics into attention.

Technical report (PDF) Interactive explainer Source on GitHub

docs.title: The idea
docs.text:
The Particle Transformer (ParT) adds a learned function of the pairwise kinematics \(U\) to the attention logits:

\[ A = \mathrm{softmax}\!\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt d} + \psi(U)\right) \]

GDS-ParT keeps two streams: particle states \(X \in \mathbb R^{B\times N\times 128}\) and a relation tensor \(R \in \mathbb R^{B\times N\times N\times 64}\) embedded from four pair features (\(\ln\Delta\), \(\ln k_T\), \(\ln z\), \(\ln m^2\)). Each particle aggregates its row of \(R\) into a summary \(s_i\). Two small MLPs map that summary to identity-initialised gates, which rescale the query and key channels before the dot product:

\[ g_i^{Q,K} = 1 + \tanh\big(\mathrm{MLP}_{Q,K}(s_i)\big) \in (0,2)^{D},\qquad q'_i = q_i \odot g_i^Q,\quad k'_j = k_j \odot g_j^K \]

The pair physics therefore changes the space in which particles compare themselves, not only the final attention scores. The reported v2 model is a hybrid. It keeps a ParT-style per-head pair bias next to the gates and pools with two class-attention blocks.

docs.title: Results (10M training jets, 1M-jet balanced test subset)
docs.text:
Model Params Test accuracy Macro AUC GDS-ParT v1 (sigmoid gates, mean pooling, 8 epochs) 1.28M 0.8272 0.9824 GDS-ParT v2 (shared gates + pair bias, 10 epochs) 2.07M 0.8484 0.9853 ParT, 10M jets (published) 2.14M 0.850 0.9860 ParticleNet, 10M jets (published) 370k 0.837 0.9837

The ParT comparison is useful context but not controlled. The published model saw about five times more jets with a different optimiser and was evaluated on the full 20M test set. Small-budget ablations show that the additive bias matters most. The difference between the gated and bias-only models is within single-seed noise. The technical report covers this in detail, together with the per-class rejections and the limitations. Full tables are in results/v2_shared_10M_10ep/RESULTS.md.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Technical report (PDF) Architecture with diagram, every equation as the code computes it, input features, gate gradients, training recipe, metrics, results, ablations, limitations and outlook. The LaTeX source is docs/GDS-ParT_Technical_Report.tex. GDS vs ParT, interactive Builds both architectures from tensors upward, with a live toy model comparing attention maps and an answered list of questions. Setup and training guide Environment, JetClass data, pipeline validation, training on a workstation or HPC cluster, ablations and reports.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Avinashistoocool/Gated-Dual-Stream-Particle-Transformer gds_part
cd gds_part
pip install -r requirements.txt
python gds_part_colab.py            # forward/backward/step sanity check on synthetic data
python train_gds_part.py --synthetic --epochs 1 --synthetic_batches 4 --batch_size 8 \
  --embed_dim 32 --n_heads 4 --n_layers 2 --ffn_dim 64 --pairwise_embed_dim 16 \
  --max_particles 32 --checkpoint_dir ./checkpoints/smoke

docs.title: Citing
docs.text: If you use GDS-ParT, cite it with GitHub's Cite this repository button, which reads CITATION.cff. Please also cite the ParT paper and the JetClass dataset: H. Qu, C. Li and S. Qian, Particle Transformer for Jet Tagging, ICML 2022, arXiv:2202.03772.

docs.title: Setup and training guide
docs.text:
Note

This page renders GUIDE.md from the repository root. Paths such as checkpoints/ and results/ are relative to a clone of the repository.

docs.title: GDS-ParT setup guide: lab workstation, HPC cluster, Colab
docs.text: This guide explains how to get the repository running on a new machine, check that the setup is correct, and launch training or evaluation. The same code runs everywhere. Only the paths and the GPU-memory settings change between machines.

docs.title: 0. Requirements
docs.text:
Minimum Recommended GPU NVIDIA, 6 GB (laptop RTX 4050 works) 24–80 GB (RTX 4090/A100/H100) RAM 16 GB 32 GB+ Disk ~25 GB (10M train + 1M val + 1M test ROOT files + cache) NVMe/local scratch for the cache Python 3.10+ 3.11 CUDA driver anything that supports your torch wheel (nvidia-smi)

Disk usage for each split is about 1.5 GB of ROOT files per 1M jets, plus about 1.9 GB of cache per 1M jets.

docs.title: 1. Get the code
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Avinashistoocool/Gated-Dual-Stream-Particle-Transformer gds_part
cd gds_part

The repository does not contain caches, and normally no checkpoints (*.pt). To continue an existing run on another machine, copy its checkpoints/<run>/last.pt and train with --resume and the same --checkpoint_dir.

Exception: the 20-epoch 10M run is committed so it can be resumed from a clone. checkpoints/v2_shared_10M_20ep/last.pt holds the state after epoch 8 of 20 (val acc 0.8473, model + EMA + optimizer + scheduler + history). To continue it, point $DATA at your JetClass folder (train_10M, val, test; see section 3) and run:

python train_gds_part.py --train $DATA/train_10M --val $DATA/val --test $DATA/test \
  --cache_dir $DATA/cache --epochs 20 --batch_size 512 --lr 1e-3 \
  --per_layer_gate 0 --ema_decay 0.9999 --log_every 500 \
  --checkpoint_dir ./checkpoints/v2_shared_10M_20ep --resume

Keep --epochs 20, --batch_size 512 and the model flags unchanged, otherwise the LR schedule or the checkpoint will not match. The first run on a new machine rebuilds the cache in --cache_dir. The finished 10-epoch model (test acc 0.8484, AUC 0.9853) is in checkpoints/v2_shared_10M_10ep/best.pt, with its report in results/v2_shared_10M_10ep/.

docs.title: Lab workstation (Linux or Windows)
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv
# Linux:   source .venv/bin/activate
# Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install --upgrade pip
# choose the wheel that matches your driver: cu121 / cu124 / cu128
pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: HPC cluster (conda + modules)
docs.text:
bash hpc/setup_env.sh          # creates conda env "gds" and installs everything

To change the CUDA wheel, edit the --index-url line in hpc/setup_env.sh. Run setup on the login node, because compute nodes usually have no internet access.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))"
python gds_part_colab.py       # forward/backward/step sanity check -> "SANITY CHECK PASSED"
python train_gds_part.py --synthetic --epochs 1 --synthetic_batches 4 --batch_size 8 \
  --embed_dim 32 --n_heads 4 --n_layers 2 --ffn_dim 64 --pairwise_embed_dim 16 \
  --max_particles 32 --checkpoint_dir ./checkpoints/smoke

docs.title: 3. Get JetClass data
docs.text:
$DATA is any folder you choose; it is not a fixed path. Set it before running the commands, for example export DATA=/data/$USER/JetClass (Linux) or $env:DATA="D:\JetClass" (PowerShell). Under it the trainer expects:

$DATA/
├── train_10M/   # 100 ROOT files, 10 per class (~14 GB)
├── val/         # 10 ROOT files (~1.4 GB)
├── test/        # 10 ROOT files (~1.4 GB)
└── cache/       # created by the trainer (~25 GB for the splits above)

Option A: copy from a machine that already has it (fastest). Copy train_10M, val and test (about 17 GB). You can also copy cache (about 25 GB) to skip the 20–40 min conversion. The cache directory names include the split folder name (for example cache/train_train_10M_all_128), so keep the folder names unchanged if you copy the cache.

rsync -avP user@laptop:/path/to/JetClass/ $DATA/          # or copy from an external drive

Option B: download from Zenodo. Each JetClass ROOT file contains 100k jets of one class. fetch_jetclass_subset.py downloads only the files you request from Zenodo, using HTTP range reads, so you do not need to download the full 190 GB tarballs.

# 10M train (10 files/class), 1M val, 1M test  -> $DATA/{train,val,test}
python data/fetch_jetclass_subset.py --out $DATA --train_files 10 --val_files 1 --test_files 1
mv $DATA/train $DATA/train_10M      # match the folder name used by the committed 20-epoch run
# quick experiments: --train_files 1  (1M jets)

On HPC, use the scratch filesystem rather than $HOME, which has a small quota. Run the download on the login node or a data-transfer node:

DATA=/scratch/$USER/JetClass bash hpc/setup_env.sh data

When a split is first used, the trainer converts it into a ragged on-disk cache under --cache_dir. For 10M jets this takes 20–40 min of CPU time, and later runs reuse the cache. Caches are portable between machines because they are plain numpy memmaps, so you can rsync $DATA/cache to skip the conversion step.

docs.title: 4. Validate the pipeline (strongly recommended on a new machine)
docs.text:
This step runs the official pretrained ParT on your cached test data, using this repo's preprocessing and metric code. If the result matches the paper, your data, features, and metrics are correct.

pip install --no-deps weaver-core==0.4.17   # 0.5.x is incompatible with the released weights
curl -L -o ParT_full.pt https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jet-universe/particle_transformer/main/models/ParT_full.pt
python train_gds_part.py --train $DATA/train --val $DATA/val --test $DATA/test \
  --cache_dir $DATA/cache --cache_only --checkpoint_dir ./checkpoints/cache_only
python validate_pipeline.py --ckpt ParT_full.pt --cache $DATA/cache/test_test_all_128 --max_jets 200000

Expected output: accuracy ≈ 0.861 and AUC ≈ 0.9877. On 2026-10-19 the reference laptop measured 0.8612 / 0.9877 on 200k jets. Rejection values at high efficiency are noisy on small test sets.

docs.title: Lab workstation
docs.text:
python train_gds_part.py \
  --train $DATA/train --val $DATA/val --test $DATA/test --cache_dir $DATA/cache \
  --epochs 20 --batch_size 512 --lr 1e-3 \
  --max_pairs_per_step 8000000 --gpu_mem_fraction 1 \
  --checkpoint_dir ./checkpoints/v2_10M
# add --resume to continue after interruption
Knob Meaning Guidance --max_pairs_per_step upper limit on B·N² for each forward pass. Larger batches are split into micro-batches with gradient accumulation (the effective batch size stays the same) 2M for 6 GB, 4–8M for 24 GB, 8–16M for 40–80 GB --gpu_mem_fraction upper limit on PyTorch's share of VRAM Keep 0.8 on Windows to avoid a ~4× slowdown from WDDM spilling into shared memory. Use 1 on Linux --epochs passes over the train set With 10M jets, the curve is still rising at epoch 8 (see results/). Use ≥ 20 --jets_per_class subsample train for quick experiments

Monitor the run with tail -f checkpoints/v2_10M/train.log, or with python monitor_training.py --log checkpoints/v2_10M/train.log.

docs.title: HPC: PBS/Torque
docs.text:
# first edit the #PBS queue/resources and the module lines in hpc/train_pbs.sh
qsub -v DATA=/scratch/$USER/JetClass,EPOCHS=20,RUN=./checkpoints/v2_10M hpc/train_pbs.sh
qstat -u $USER

docs.title: HPC: SLURM
docs.text:
# first edit #SBATCH -p / --gres / modules in hpc/train_slurm.sh
sbatch --export=ALL,DATA=/scratch/$USER/JetClass,EPOCHS=20,RUN=./checkpoints/v2_10M hpc/train_slurm.sh
squeue -u $USER

Both job scripts pass --resume. If a job reaches its walltime limit, resubmit the same command with the same RUN and training continues from last.pt (the optimizer, scheduler, and EMA state are restored as well). To pass any other trainer flag, use EXTRA="--n_layers 8 --pair_bias 1".

The first job builds the cache. If your cluster limits CPU time on GPU nodes, build the cache beforehand in a CPU job with --cache_only.

docs.title: 6. Ablations
docs.text:
python run_ablations.py --train $DATA/train --val $DATA/val --cache_dir $DATA/cache \
  --jets_per_class 100000 --epochs 3 --out ./ablations
python run_ablations.py ... --only v2_full,no_gate   # run a subset of variants

For short runs (fewer than ~20k steps), add --extra "--ema_decay 0", because an EMA with decay 0.999 lags behind and distorts the comparison. Summaries of the 2026-10-19 runs (with and without EMA) are in results/ablation_summaries/.

Every variant uses the same data and optimizer, and the script writes ablations/ABLATIONS.md. Completed variants are skipped when you run it again. Variants:

Name What changes v1 original model: shared sigmoid gate, mean pooling, 6 layers v2_full current default no_gate v2 without Q/K gates, which is ParT-style bias-only attention. This is the control for "do the gates help?" no_pair_bias v2 with gates only shared_gate v2 with one uniform gate shared across layers v1_plus_cls v1 + class-attention pooling

docs.title: 7. Evaluate and report
docs.text:
When training finishes, the trainer evaluates best.pt on val and test and writes results.json and {val,test}_predictions.npz. Then run:

python make_report.py --run_dir ./checkpoints/v2_10M   # plots + RESULTS.md with ParT-paper table

docs.title: 8. Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix CUDA out of memory lower --max_pairs_per_step (training uses this value; evaluation uses 2× it) Very slow on Windows, GPU "shared memory" usage growing keep --gpu_mem_fraction 0.8 no files for <class> while building the cache the directory must contain <Prefix>_NNN.root files (e.g. HToBB_120.root). Check --train Changed --max_particles / --jets_per_class a new cache directory is created automatically. Old caches can be deleted Validation gives garbage (~10% acc) wrong weaver-core version. Use 0.4.17 Resume complains about missing keys the architecture flags must match the run that produced last.pt (see args in the checkpoint)
